skill.name: playwright-browser
skill.description: Control a Playwright browser from CLI commands to navigate pages, inspect accessibility snapshots, click elements, type text, and capture screenshots.
skill.summary: Automates browser navigation, interaction, snapshots, and screenshots through Playwright CLI commands.
skill.author: Bind

security_audit.summary: The static external command findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences and inline backticks in usage documentation. The hardcoded URLs are documented navigation examples, not hidden network endpoints. A semantic privacy issue remains because the skill documents persistent browser data that can retain cookies and localStorage.

remediation.issue: Persistent browser state can store sensitive cookies and localStorage.
remediation.suggestion: Document a cleanup workflow, add a command or option to purge .playwright-data/, and advise users to avoid production credentials in shared projects.

remediation.issue: The reviewed package does not include the referenced implementation scripts.
remediation.suggestion: Publish the Playwright command source with the skill so reviewers and users can verify browser behavior and storage handling.

remediation.issue: Browser automation can interact with untrusted pages.
remediation.suggestion: Recommend trusted test sites, isolated browser profiles, and least-privilege test accounts for routine automation.

semantic_findings.title: Persistent Browser Profile Stores Session Data
semantic_findings.description: SKILL.md states that browser data is stored in .playwright-data/ and that cookies and localStorage persist between sessions. This can retain sensitive authenticated session data in a project directory if users browse private sites.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The documentation directly describes persistent cookie and localStorage behavior. The implementation files were not present in the scanned package, so the exact storage controls could not be verified.

content.value_statement: Manual browser checks slow down UI testing and debugging. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through Playwright navigation, snapshots, clicks, typing, and screenshots.
actual_capabilities: Starts, stops, and checks a persistent Playwright browser session.
Navigates the active browser to a supplied URL.
Reads the current page accessibility tree for element discovery.
Types text into elements and can press a follow-up key.
Clicks elements by role, text, or CSS selector reference.
Captures page screenshots, including full-page screenshots.
limitations: Requires Bun, Playwright, and the referenced CLI scripts to be available.
The reviewed package contains documentation and a manifest, not implementation source.
Persistent browser state may store cookies and localStorage in .playwright-data/.
Element actions depend on resolvable roles, text, or CSS selectors.

use_cases.title: Verify UI Flows
use_cases.description: Run repeatable page navigation, typing, clicking, and screenshot steps during feature development.

use_cases.title: Inspect Accessibility Structure
use_cases.description: Review the accessibility tree before choosing reliable element references for automation.

use_cases.title: Capture Web Evidence
use_cases.description: Navigate a browser session and save screenshots for bug reports or release checks.

prompt_templates.title: Open a Page
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Playwright browser skill to start a session, open the target URL, and confirm the page title or main heading.

prompt_templates.title: Find an Element
prompt_templates.prompt: Open the page, capture the accessibility snapshot, and identify the best role or text reference for the primary action button.

prompt_templates.title: Exercise a Form
prompt_templates.prompt: Navigate to the form page, fill the requested fields with test data, submit the form, and report the visible result.

prompt_templates.title: Document a Regression
prompt_templates.prompt: Reproduce the reported issue in a persistent session, collect snapshots before and after the interaction, and save a full-page screenshot.

output_examples.input: Check whether the search page can submit a query and show results.
output_examples.output: The assistant opens the page, finds the search box from the accessibility tree, enters the query, submits it, and summarizes the result state.

output_examples.input: Capture visual evidence for a layout bug on a product page.
output_examples.output: The assistant navigates to the page, waits for loading, captures a screenshot, and reports where the image was saved.

output_examples.input: Identify a reliable selector for the sign-in button.
output_examples.output: The assistant reads the accessibility snapshot and recommends the most stable role or text reference for the button.

best_practices: Use accessibility role and name references before CSS selectors when possible.
Use isolated test accounts and avoid sensitive production sessions.
Clear persistent browser data after testing private or authenticated pages.
anti_patterns: Do not enter real credentials into untrusted or unknown websites.
Do not rely on fragile CSS selectors when accessible names are available.
Do not commit screenshots or browser profile data that may contain private information.

faq.question: What does this skill control?
faq.answer: It controls a Playwright browser through documented CLI commands for navigation, snapshots, typing, clicks, and screenshots.

faq.question: Does it support Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report marks the skill as compatible with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: How does it find page elements?
faq.answer: It recommends using the accessibility tree, then selecting elements by role and name, text, or CSS selector.

faq.question: Can it keep users signed in?
faq.answer: The documentation says the persistent context keeps cookies and localStorage between sessions.

faq.question: What should users protect?
faq.answer: Users should protect browser profile data, screenshots, test credentials, and any content viewed during automation.

faq.question: What dependencies are expected?
faq.answer: The skill expects Playwright, Bun, and the referenced command scripts to be available in the working environment.
